system: You are the lead AI reviewer (orchestrator) on a deal team. Your cheap parser subagents have read the data room and returned the compact findings below. Compile a concise DD summary for the partner: key findings, red flags, and a clear recommendation on whether to proceed.

exchanges.user:
===== PARSER FINDINGS =====
| Document | What it is | Deal-team notes |
|---|---|---|
| **L01 – NDA** | Mutual NDA with Halden Partners. | Two-year term; standard carve-outs; no non-solicit. |
| **L02 – Lease** | Five-year head-office lease beginning in 2024. | Market rent review in year three. Landlord consent required for assignment, but change of control is expressly not an assignment. |
| **L03 – Management accounts** | FY revenue and gross-margin summary. | Revenue AUD 18.4m, up 9%; gross margin 61%. Arlen Health is highly concentrated at 41% of revenue; next-largest customer is 7%. |
| **L04 – HR** | Headcount and employment information. | 94 employees on standard contracts. CTO and Head of Sales have 12-month retention letters; review terms and any transaction-related conditions. |
| **L05 – Arlen Health contract** | Five-year MSA renewed 1 July 2025 for platform, hosting and support. | Key concentration and transaction risk: Arlen (41% of revenue) can terminate for convenience, without a fee, on 90 days’ notice during the six months after a supplier change of control. Annual CPI-indexed fees are billed quarterly in advance. 99.9% monthly uptime; service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. Liability capped at 12 months’ fees, except data breaches at 3× annual fees. Australian data hosting and maintained ISO 27001 certification. Either party may terminate for uncured material breach after 30 days. Confirm change-of-control trigger, notice mechanics, and operational/compliance status. |
| **L06 – Bank facility** | AUD 6m revolving facility with Southgate Bank, expiring 2027. | Quarterly net-debt/EBITDA covenant capped at 2.5×; assess compliance and any waiver or consent requirements. |
| **L07 – CFO email** | Internal email to the Chair dated 14 April. | CFO says the 31 March leverage test was breached (2.9× vs. 2.5×); bank had not yet been notified, with notification planned after the board meeting. Urgent diligence item: establish current status, lender notice, waiver, and any default or drawstop consequences. |
| **L08 – Customer Success note** | Internal observation about small-business churn. | Possible link to January price change is explicitly uncertain; numbers are small and it is too early to conclude. Treat as an unverified trend; request cohort/retention data. |
| **L09 – Insurance** | PI and cyber insurance summary. | AUD 10m cover, renewed in March; no notified claims. Confirm policy limits, exclusions, and continuity/claims history as needed. |
| **L10 – IP** | Platform code ownership and open-source components. | Employee code is covered by standard IP assignments. MIT and Apache 2.0 components are generally permissive; verify notices, attribution, and any modifications/distribution obligations. |
| **L11 – Supplier** | Cloud-hosting arrangement on standard online terms. | Major provider, monthly billing, no minimum commitment. Review service, data, security, termination, and change-of-control terms in the online terms. |
| **L12 – Board minutes** | Board minutes dated 20 March. | FY budget and hiring plan approved; strong sales pipeline noted. No other business recorded. |
| **L13 – Privacy policy** | Privacy policy and training summary. | Updated for 2025 amendments; annual staff privacy training completed. Verify implementation and any incidents or outstanding compliance actions. |
| **L14 – Vendor contract** | Office-cleaning contract. | 12-month term; terminable on 30 days’ notice. |
| **L15 – Fixed assets** | Laptops and office fit-out. | Written-down value AUD 0.4m. |

Write the DD summary now.
exchanges.text:
## DD summary — conditional proceed

**Recommendation:** Proceed with focused diligence, but **do not commit unconditionally** until the Arlen change-of-control exposure and bank covenant breach are resolved. These are material revenue and financing risks.

### Key findings and red flags
- **Critical customer risk (L03/L05):** Arlen accounts for **41% of revenue (~AUD 7.5m)** and may terminate without a fee on 90 days’ notice during the six months following a supplier change of control. The five-year renewal does not protect against this exit. Confirm trigger and notice mechanics; seek an enforceable waiver or other satisfactory contractual protection before closing.
- **Reported covenant breach (L06/L07):** The CFO reported 31 March leverage of **2.9× versus a 2.5× limit**; the bank had not been notified as of the 14 April email. Current status is unknown. Obtain lender correspondence, updated covenant calculations and any written waiver; establish default, drawstop and transaction-consent implications.
- **Trading (L03/L08):** Revenue is **AUD 18.4m, up 9%, with 61% gross margin**. These figures do not establish EBITDA or cash conversion. Small-business churn concerns remain unverified; obtain cohort retention data before attributing churn to January pricing.
- **Operational and liability exposure (L05/L09/L11/L13):** Arlen requires Australian hosting, maintained ISO 27001 certification and 99.9% monthly uptime; data-breach liability is capped at **3× annual fees**. Verify compliance, incidents, hosting terms and whether AUD 10m insurance meaningfully covers the relevant exposures.
- **People and IP (L04/L10):** Review CTO and Head of Sales retention letters for transaction conditions. Employee IP assignments and permissive open-source licences are reassuring, subject to ownership and licence-compliance verification.
- **Other items:** Lease change of control expressly does not constitute assignment; year-three market rent review remains a budgeting consideration. No other comparable red flags emerge from the summaries.

### Required path to closing
Resolve lender default/waiver status and secure acceptable Arlen protection; validate earnings, cash conversion and retention; complete targeted compliance, insurance and key-person diligence. **If Arlen exposure remains unresolved, reassess valuation and deal structure—or decline if the downside is unacceptable.**

*Based on parser summaries only; underlying documents and current status remain to be verified.*
